dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: If I'm not tailing some husband who's having an affair, I'm looking for earrings that someone lost on the road... If this is all a detective does, I'd be better off changing careers...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is work not going so well?

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Real gift for understatement you've got. There's so little of it going around that "work" is turning into an occasional pastime.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: *sigh* Around here, even if a big case does occur, people would rather just round up all the suspects and "interrogate" them with the butt of a weapon than get a real detective to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: You'd be amazed how many criminals they end up catching — a decent chunk more than the number of people who actually commit any crimes, I'd wager.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I take it you haven't gotten any big cases lately?

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Well, I mean, I guess, if you count... Not long ago, I helped a merchant from Sumeru find their lost Sumpter Beast. It fell asleep curled up down an alleyway.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: The Sumpter Beast was pretty big... So, I guess you could say that means the case was big too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you want to change careers?

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Detectives aren't very popular in Nod-Krai. The only cases I get are for very minor problems.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: I often dream of cracking a really big case — pinpointing the one tiny hole in an otherwise airtight act of criminality... But now I'm starting to think that instead of dreaming about it, I should be writing it all down and turning it into a detective novel!

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: At least in Nod-Krai, being a crime novelist sounds a lot more appealing than being a detective.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: In fact, I already have some ideas. You look like you've seen a few things. Why not be my first test audience?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye, and good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Goodbye, and good luck to you, too! That was the most touching blessing I've heard in quite some time. *sigh* I do hope that things start going well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm more of a non-fiction fan...

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Really? Well, that's a shame...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure thing. I'm all ears.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Alright, first up is "The Rifthound of the Bashkirovs."

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: The central conceit is this — a family who raises Rifthounds uses them to open rifts to a secret room where they can carry out murders without leaving a trace!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why not just let the Rifthounds do the murdering?

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Erm... That's a good question... Maybe I was too focused on explaining how the family could open the secret room... Alright, how about this one — "The Bakufu Food Taster Murders"

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: A food taster for the Yashiro Commission uses their position to put poison in some Tricolor Dango personally prepared by the Shogun in an attempt to assassinate the head of the Commission...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe we can skip this one...

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Really? Hmm... Is the concept not exciting enough? I could always refine it a little...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think they'd be able to taste the food...

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Oh? I think I see what you're getting at... There's no way a food taster would be allowed to touch something made by the Shogun themselves, as that would be seen as disrespecting the latter, correct? I guess I need to brush up on Inazuman culture.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: I'm amazed how much you know about these things! Alright, this one's a surefire hit — "The Curious Case of the Liyue Bulle Fruit"!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bulle Fruit don't grow in Liyue...

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Oh, really? I always thought Bulle Fruit were a Liyue specialty...

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: *sigh* I thought my fantasies would make for exciting detective novels, but it looks like becoming a crime writer isn't any easier than being an actual detective...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe we can skip this one...

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Really? *sigh* It looks like becoming a crime writer isn't any easier than being an actual detective...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (<color=#FFCC33FF>Jahoda</color> appears to have something on her mind...)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hey, Mr. Hjerson! We've found the novel you asked us to look for the last time. We'll have it sent it over to you when we get the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Hjerson
dialogues.text: Really? Thank you so much. Once I'm done with my mystery novel, you'll be the first to read it!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Sure... Sounds good...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (A mystery novel, he said? Um, I don't really understand those... Maybe I'll give this one to Ineffa, she'll definitely enjoy it more than I will.)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Huh? Why isn't Hjerson saying anything now? Is he already thinking about the plot? Oh well, I'd better leave quietly...)
